From a claim to a DeepProbLog verdict

Inspect the input claim, automatic parse, shared arguments, frozen-model scores, compiled program, and an actual training update.

Paper designGenerated examplesImplementation

This is an executed development prototype. The earlier two-example training run fits a 643-parameter score calibrator. The new visual/audio feature audit extracts media-conditioned representations and runs separate evidence trees; its feature-based classifiers are not trained yet. View the checklist. The real-claim audit measures compiler coverage and reviews accepted programs. The new compilation approaches tab compares trained SRL, pretrained AMR and neural graph generation on fixed development claims. Compilation is the current priority; further media verification and relation training are deferred. The earlier compiler improvements remain available for comparison.

Download source and cached inputsFull traces (JSON)Executed learned programAutomated test results

Real video: attribute binding

These shorter claims come from the inspected aircraft/bus color pair. The input sentence is parsed automatically. Six frozen Qwen3-VL-8B observations are reused from 15 October; no new GPU calls were needed. The aircraft and bus-group references are specified manually.

Original color assignments

1

Input claim and reference label

The aircraft is gray and the school buses are yellow.

Reference label: supported. assistant inspection of source frames; development labels, not human gold.

2

Parse and semantic structure

3

Compiled predicates

X1 and X2 are claim participant variables; E1 is an event variable when present. A repeated variable must keep the same evidence assignment. Candidate IDs are lookup keys, not classifier features.

(EXISTS X1: ((entity(X1, aircraft) AND attribute(X1, gray))) AND EXISTS X2: ((entity(X2, school_bus) AND attribute(X2, yellow))))
Table 1. Predicates compiled automatically from this claim. A relation is scored as a complete ordered tuple.
IDPredicateArgument rolesFunction
a0entity(X1, aircraft)referent=X1, type=aircraftfixed
a1attribute(X1, gray)holder=X1, property=graylearnable
a2entity(X2, school_bus)referent=X2, type=school_busfixed
a3attribute(X2, yellow)holder=X2, property=yellowlearnable

Controlled test: keep both roles in the same event

Constructed evidence, not video predictions. This inventory contains two events: Alice hugs Bob; Carol hugs Dave. It tests the compiler and inference separately from perception.

All four people are present and hugging occurs. Alice hugging Dave still lacks a matching event. The complete relation is evaluated separately for each candidate event; agent and object cannot select different events.

The program combines probabilities under its stated model assumptions. Different queries to the same perception model are treated as independent here unless they reuse the exact same canonical observation. This assumption does not guarantee calibrated probabilities.

Sample training through DeepProbLog

This is a training demonstration on two development claims from one video. One has the supported aircraft/bus colors; the other swaps the colors. Both labels come from assistant inspection. The same claims are shown before and after training. There is no held-out accuracy result.

The entity observations and logical rules are fixed. A 64-hidden-unit multilayer perceptron adjusts each attribute relation’s three probabilities. Its six inputs are the three frozen scores and their logarithms; it receives no claim IDs, candidate IDs, or target labels. It therefore acts mainly as a learned score calibrator in this first run.

For one claim, the loss is:

\[\mathcal{L}(\theta)=-\log p_{\theta}(y)\]

Here \(y\) is the reference claim label, \(p_{\theta}(y)\) is its probability returned by DeepProbLog, and \(\theta\) denotes the small classifier’s weights. Training averages this loss across claims. The reference labels supervise the final verdict; no local attribute labels are supplied to the training loop.

Compiler and inference checks

23 automated semantic, probability, and training tests; 0 failures. Tests include active/passive role equivalence, shared subjects, negation scope, branch-local references, duplicated evidence, overlapping proofs, unavailable evidence, bounded candidates, and actual gradient updates.

Corrections made during implementation

  • Event existence stays inside the scope of clause negation.
  • Participant variables are bound where their uses meet. A disjunction does not require candidates for an unused branch.
  • DeepProbLog 2.0.6’s near-zero/near-one simplification is overridden locally: only exact constants are identities. Double precision preserves very small probability outcomes and gradients.
  • Canonical observations are shared across duplicate predicates and alternative proofs.
  • Missing observations and incomplete candidate coverage yield explicit unknown states.

The probability tests compare DeepProbLog with an independent enumeration of categorical outcomes. Every displayed verdict distribution is checked to sum to one within one billionth, without renormalizing the backend output.

Current limits

  • Restricted English claims only. Quantified counts, unresolved pronouns, temporal/causal clauses, and source-assertion scope are rejected.
  • Real-media candidates are manually specified depicted referents; there is no automatic tracker in this demonstration.
  • The color relations are learned; the controlled event table only tests shared-event reasoning.
  • Perception scores are uncalibrated, and dependence between different model questions is not estimated.
  • This original CPU demonstration used no audio. The new Visual and audio tab reports a separate frozen-feature pilot; no multimodal-model fine-tuning or held-out evaluation has been run.

Frozen features and separate visual/audio trees

Executed development pilot. We extracted real neural representations for 12 propositions under four input conditions in each modality: 96 forward passes in the final audit. The main clip and one unrelated clip are development examples. Features are cached for later learning; the tree inference below still uses frozen-model A/B/C scores. No new classifier was trained and no held-out accuracy is reported.

Main limitation found: the audio verifier gives high music support even to silence and text alone. The default chat template fixes the unusable description but does not fix this control failure. The extracted vectors need further checks before training, and the audio model’s proposed labels must not be treated as gold.

Feature measurementsComplete tree tracesExecuted DeepProbLog programEdit review and reference labelsSource and cached feature replayCurrent test results

1. Inspect the evidence before choosing an edit

The main excerpt is the first 12 seconds of the existing aircraft/bus clip. The visual model receives three cached frames at indices 0, 5 and 10; the audio model receives the 12-second waveform and no frames or transcript. Cached frame indices are nominal sampling times, not independently certified event boundaries. The same window is used for both modalities.

S = supported, R = refuted, U = insufficient evidence. These are development reference labels, separate from the model predictions. An audio-only color claim stays U; a silent-frame music claim stays U. The mixed claims require both clauses, but do not require them to occur at the same instant.

3. Extract media-conditioned features, before an answer

The new feature is the final decoder representation at the last prompt token. It is a vector computed from the complete proposition and the attached frames or waveform, before generating an answer. For example, “aircraft is gray” and “school buses are gray” specify different property holders. The target label and paired claim are never included. This is a standard frozen neural representation, rather than the earlier six inputs made from three scores and their logarithms.

Table 30. Actual models and feature dimensions, read from the saved tensors. The models remain frozen.
BranchFrozen modelInput and selected representationMeasured size

Audioqwen3-omni/30B-A3B-Instruct12-second waveform + proposition2048 floating-point values per proposition

What is ready: cached proposition-conditioned vectors, complete prompts, input shapes, media hashes, and control measurements. Still to do: implement and train a linear classifier and a small MLP on source-video-disjoint data. These vectors summarize the supplied clip; they are not object-box or speaker-track features. Alternative real entity/event assignments and candidate-localized features still need a larger pilot.

Each proposition was run with matched media, an unrelated clothing/stadium clip, blank media of the same shape and duration, and text alone. Matched versus blank retains the exact prompt and token sequence, changing only media content. Text alone removes the media placeholders, so it is a useful diagnostic but not a perfectly matched intervention. An unrelated clip is not automatically a negative example: it may contain the same sound.

Audio template check and failed controls

The initial audio run inserted an empty thinking block. Its main-clip description was whitespace only, and several blank/text-only music questions received high support. We repeated the readouts with the checkpoint’s documented default chat template. The free-text inspection also received an explicit stop token and repetition penalty; its improvement cannot be attributed to the template alone. Observed source error: the silent-frame model assigns 99.68% support to “The narrator mentions Alaska,” despite a prompt that excludes captions as speech evidence. That probability remains visible above. This prediction is ineligible under the declared evidence policy: silent frames cannot certify exact spoken words. The claim compiler now rejects “mention” until source/content scope is represented correctly, rather than requiring Alaska to be physically present. Full speech-assertion compilation remains future work.

4. Compile two evidence trees and combine corresponding predicates

The compiler supplies one logical form and semantic roles. The visual and audio trees reuse that structure but have distinct observations and verdicts. This pilot uses manually selected referents: the depicted aircraft, the bus group, and the music track. The candidate domain is explicitly limited to those selected referents; this is not automatic tracking or a complete inventory of every possible event.

The fixed policy assigns depicted color predicates to visual evidence and music predicates to sound evidence. Ineligible sources contribute U, while their raw outputs are retained in the audit. We combine evidence for each predicate with the same candidate assignment, then run the claim’s AND/OR/NOT rules. We do not take the maximum of the two whole-claim scores.

Table 34. Fixed, symmetric evidence-combination rule for sources that mean the same proposition. A source assertion and direct event evidence are not interchangeable. Source disagreements remain visible in the diagnostic trace.
First sourceSecond sourceCombined stateMeaning
SUSOne eligible source supplies support
RUROne eligible source supplies refutation
SSSAgreement
RRRAgreement
SRU + conflict diagnosticDo not silently choose a source
UUUNo sufficient evidence

In these diagrams, X1 is the selected aircraft and X2 is the selected music track. entity checks presence/type under the declared source policy; attribute checks a property attached to that same referent. The two clauses concern different referents. This example does not test whether a visible person is the source of a particular voice; automatic audio-visual identity matching remains open.

5. Checks and limits

28 automated tests pass. The new tests cover complementary evidence when both separate roots are unknown, support/refutation conflicts, ineligible-source exclusion with raw scores retained, and candidate-identity alignment. Every displayed root agrees with independent categorical-world enumeration within one ten-billionth and sums to one within one billionth.

Probability aggregation still assumes independent local observations except where canonical keys explicitly share them. Repeated questions to the same frozen model can be correlated; these probabilities are not calibrated confidence guarantees. The conflict examples in the automated tests use stipulated inputs, not observed cross-modal contradictions in this clip.

Tense and aspect: baseline gap and new prototype

The frozen v1 compiler drops these distinctions. The six-sentence diagnostic below records the unchanged baseline. The new semantic compiler now emits distinct temporal predicates and tests them with supplied event-time annotations. It does not yet infer temporal observations from real media.

Table 39. Executed diagnostic on the unchanged compiler. All four spacecraft clauses produce the same predicates. Both Apollo 11 clauses hit the generic counting guard on the numeral in the name; their locations are not yet compiled either.
ClaimObserved compiler result
Apollo 11 landed on the moon.Rejected: Counting and quantified noun phrases are outside the initial fragment.
Apollo 11 is landing on the moon.Rejected: Counting and quantified noun phrases are outside the initial fragment.
The spacecraft landed.EXISTS X1: ((entity(X1, spacecraft) AND EXISTS E1: ((event(E1, land) AND land(E1, X1)))))
The spacecraft is landing.EXISTS X1: ((entity(X1, spacecraft) AND EXISTS E1: ((event(E1, land) AND land(E1, X1)))))
The spacecraft was landing.EXISTS X1: ((entity(X1, spacecraft) AND EXISTS E1: ((event(E1, land) AND land(E1, X1)))))

Download exact parses, compiler outputs, versions and hashes.

Interpretation and implementation scope: tense locates an event relative to a context-dependent reference time; aspect describes how the event unfolds. The reference time may come from the narration or the depicted scene, rather than today’s date. Extract English tense/aspect from the auxiliary sequence as well as the main verb: “was landing” is past progressive even though “landing” itself has a present-participle tag.

Table 40. Intended distinctions. The new prototype exercises a narrow episodic interpretation with constructed intervals; it is not a general tense calculus or a real-media temporal model.
ClaimTense / aspect to preserveEvidence condition to represent
Apollo 11 landed on the moon.Past / simple, non-progressiveUnder the ordinary affirmative reading of this landing event: a completed landing before the contextual reference time. Completion depends on the event meaning, not a universal past-tense rule.
Apollo 11 is landing on the moon.Present / progressiveThe landing is in progress at the contextual reference time. This does not by itself establish a completed landing.
The spacecraft was landing.Past / progressiveThe landing was in progress at a past reference time; its completion is not guaranteed.
The spacecraft has landed.Present / perfectAn earlier landing is presented as completed and relevant at the current contextual reference time.

The new temporal predicates affect executable checks and evidence keys. Temporal questions/features from frozen media models remain to implement and evaluate. A clip showing descent may support an ongoing landing while leaving touchdown unknown. Captions or speech remain typed source evidence; an assertion is not automatically proof of world truth. Historical footage can use a present-tense narrative viewpoint, so present progressive does not automatically mean “happening now in 2026.”

A tense edit is not automatically a negative example. One clip may contain both an ongoing landing and its completion; check the intended reference time, event identity and evidence before assigning opposite labels. Window selection locates candidate evidence; tense and aspect specify what the claim requires that evidence to establish. Background definitions: UD tense, UD aspect, and the TimeML event/time specification.

How a dependency tree becomes a logical program

Beyond AND and OR: the claim compiler supports NOT and EXISTS. These are logical operations. Predicates describe what to check: entity, attribute, event, possess, and action relations such as hug. The separate visual/audio stage also uses evidence to combine two eligible observations of the same proposition.

Guide added 28 October 2026. The latest saved experiments are from 22 October: a restricted compiler, native DeepProbLog inference and sample score-calibrator training, followed by frozen visual/audio feature extraction and separate evidence trees. Feature-based classifier training, broader candidate discovery, and held-out evaluation remain pending. The examples below run the current compiler on cached or explicitly supplied parses; they add no perception experiment or accuracy claim.

1. What is fixed, and what is learned?

A Universal Dependencies (UD) tree records grammatical links between words: for example, which noun is the subject of a verb. The compiler applies fixed Python rules to these links. It creates variables for participants and events, predicates with ordered arguments, and a logical expression. No media score or reference label enters this step. A variable such as X1 stands for a participant we will later match to evidence; E1 stands for an event.

# Actual API; tokens is a list of Stanza-style UD word records.
from probabilistic_verification import ClaimCompiler
claim = ClaimCompiler().compile("example", text, tokens)
print(claim.to_dict()["logical_form"])
# Later, with a separately prepared evidence inventory:
from probabilistic_verification.logic import ground, prolog_program
program = ground(claim, evidence)
prolog, query_names = prolog_program([program], learned=False)

The saved training demonstration adjusts relation-score probabilities with a small classifier. It does not learn these grammar rules, argument roles, or truth tables. The full code is in the source ZIP; the guide’s exact inputs, outputs, and grounding trace are in compilation_guide.json.

Table 41. Logical expression operations currently implemented, with candidate binding and source combination distinguished from sentence connectives.
LayerSupported formMeaning
Claim logicAND, ORRequire all clauses, or at least one clause. OR is inclusive; both may hold.
Claim logicNOTSwap supported and refuted; preserve unknown. Restricted clause/property negation only.
Candidate bindingEXISTS X1, EXISTS E1Search supplied candidates for a participant or event satisfying the body. No universal quantifier is implemented.
Internal representationatom, constantA predicate leaf, or an explicit supported/refuted/unknown state. These are internal expression nodes, not extra English constructions.
Source combinationevidenceCombine two eligible sources for the same grounded predicate before AND/OR. Added by multimodal.py, not read from a word in the sentence.
Table 42. Predicate families emitted by compiler.py. A trainable flag enables scoring through a classifier; it does not establish that this relation has training data.
Predicate familyExampleHow the compiler creates it / scorer flag
Entity presence/typeentity(X1, alice)A noun phrase creates an entity variable and a fixed-scoring observation. “Fixed” refers to training, not certain truth.
Propertyattribute(X1, gray)A copular property (is gray) or adjective modifier (gray aircraft); trainable relation-score interface.
Event occurrence/typeevent(E1, hug)An action verb introduces an event variable and fixed-scoring occurrence observation.
Complete action relationhug(E1, X1, X2)Verb lemma becomes the predicate name; argument roles are event, agent, theme, recipient, omitting absent roles. Trainable score interface.
Possessionpossess(X2, X1)A possessive noun modifier introduces owner then possession; trainable score interface.

Action names are derived from the verb lemma rather than selected from a fixed verb list. That does not imply unrestricted verb understanding: the clause must fit the supported grammar, suitable evidence must be supplied, and assertion/intention verbs such as say, mention, and want are explicitly rejected. There are no dedicated temporal, spatial, equality, implication, XOR, or counting rules in this fragment.

2. Start with attributes and AND

The aircraft is gray and the school buses are yellow.

For “aircraft is gray,” UD makes gray the head, aircraft its nsubj (subject), and is its cop (copula). The noun becomes entity(X1, aircraft); the property becomes attribute(X1, gray). “School buses” becomes one compound noun label, school_bus. The plural does not introduce a count or universal quantification.

Table 43. Cached automatic parse for the aircraft/bus example; head 0 marks the sentence root.
WordLemmaHead word IDUD relation
1: Thethe2det
2: aircraftaircraft4nsubj
3: isbe4cop
4: graygray0root
5: andand10cc
6: thethe8det
7: schoolschool8compound
8: busesbus10nsubj
9: arebe10cop
10: yellowyellow4conj
11: ..4punct

The compiler recognizes conj plus the explicit cc word “and,” compiles each clause, and combines them. “The,” copulas, and punctuation receive explicit coverage records rather than independent evidence predicates.

(EXISTS X1: ((entity(X1, aircraft) AND attribute(X1, gray))) AND EXISTS X2: ((entity(X2, school_bus) AND attribute(X2, yellow))))

Actual copular-property rule from compiler.py:

if copular and root["upos"] in {"ADJ", "NOUN", "PROPN"}:
    body = self.add_atom("attribute", [subject_var, symbol(self.lemma(root))], "attribute",
                         ["holder", "property"], f"{subject['text']} is {root['text']}.", [root], True)
    if negators:
        body = E.negate(body)
    current = E.combine("and", [subject_expr, body])

3. Preserve who did what to whom

In “Alice hugs Bob,” nsubj maps to agent and obj to theme. A complete tuple checks one event with both participants; separate checks that Alice exists, Bob exists, and hugging occurs cannot establish this relation. In the passive “Bob is hugged by Alice,” nsubj:pass supplies the theme and obl:agent supplies the agent.

Alice hugs Bob.

EXISTS X1, X2: ((entity(X1, alice) AND entity(X2, bob) AND EXISTS E1: ((event(E1, hug) AND hug(E1, X1, X2)))))

Bob is hugged by Alice.

EXISTS X1, X2: ((entity(X1, bob) AND entity(X2, alice) AND EXISTS E1: ((event(E1, hug) AND hug(E1, X2, X1)))))

These have equivalent roles even though X1 and X2 are allocated in a different order. The action argument order is determined by this actual loop:

for role in ("agent", "theme", "recipient"):
    if role in role_tokens:
        var, noun_expr = self.noun(role_tokens[role])
        arguments.append(var)
        roles.append(role)
        argument_exprs.append(noun_expr)

iobj adds a recipient when supplied by the parse. This is a limited dependency-to-role mapping, not a general semantic-role labeling model. Ordinary locative and temporal adjuncts are not handled. See the Same-event test for the constructed Alice/Bob versus Alice/Dave candidate example.

4. Negation, possession, OR, and shared names

Expand an example to see its exact generated logical form and input UD records. The first three use saved automatic parses. The OR/shared-name examples use hand-specified parses to isolate compiler behavior: the existing automatic parser misreads “waves” in three saved regression cases.

Alice does not hug Bob.

NOT surrounds the entire event search. It does not mean that one nonmatching event is enough to support the negative claim.

Input: saved automatic Stanza parse.

EXISTS X1, X2: ((entity(X1, alice) AND entity(X2, bob) AND NOT (EXISTS E1: ((event(E1, hug) AND hug(E1, X1, X2))))))

For event negation, entity-presence checks remain outside NOT, while event occurrence and the complete relation stay inside NOT(EXISTS E1: ...). For “not yellow,” only the attribute is negated. Negation of an unknown observation remains unknown; missing evidence cannot prove the negative claim. The code rejects negative indefinite arguments such as “A woman does not wear a shirt,” whose quantifier scope needs richer analysis.

bind_references() puts an entity’s EXISTS where its uses meet. Branch-only participants stay within their OR branch. Repeated proper names share a variable; repeated common nouns are not automatically resolved as the same object. Coordinated noun arguments such as “Alice and Bob hug Carol” are rejected because collective versus separate actions are unresolved.

5. Replace variables with supplied evidence candidates

This step is called grounding: substitute concrete candidate IDs for variables. EXISTS is expanded into OR over assignments. Candidates are supplied separately; the prototype does not detect or track them automatically. The following trace uses Alice/Bob and two candidate hugging events, with no perception observations supplied.

evidence = Evidence(
    media_id="guide_clip",
    domains={"X1": ["alice_candidate"], "X2": ["bob_candidate"],
             "E1": ["hug_one", "hug_two"]},
    complete={"X1": True, "X2": True, "E1": False},
    observations={},
)
program = ground(claim, evidence)  # claim is the active Alice/Bob example

For each event, the body checks event(hug_one, hug) and hug(hug_one, alice_candidate, bob_candidate), then repeats for hug_two. One event variable ties all roles together. An incomplete event inventory adds an unknown alternative: no matching event among the listed candidates is insufficient for refutation. A declared complete inventory permits refutation when every assignment is refuted. Candidate expansion has a default limit of 256; exceeding it raises an error.

Actual EXISTS expansion in logic.py:

domains = [evidence.domains.get(v, []) for v in expr.variables]
if any(len(d) != len(set(d)) for d in domains):
    raise ValueError("Candidate domains must not contain duplicate IDs.")
count = math.prod(map(len, domains))
if budget + count > max_expansions:
    raise ValueError(f"Candidate expansion exceeds the explicit limit of {max_expansions}.")
complete = all(evidence.complete.get(v, False) for v in expr.variables)
expansions.append(dict(variables=list(expr.variables), candidate_combinations=count,
                       complete=complete, outer_assignment=dict(assignment)))
branches = []
for values in itertools.product(*domains):
    budget += 1
    branches.append(visit(expr.children[0], dict(assignment, **dict(zip(expr.variables, values)))))
if not complete:
    branches.append(E.constant("unknown"))
return E.combine("or", branches)

An observation’s identity contains media ID, evidence route, predicate name, and all substituted arguments. Exact reuse shares one categorical random variable, including across different proof paths; duplicated evidence does not become an independent second observation.

["guide_clip","visual_depiction","hug",["hug_one","alice_candidate","bob_candidate"]]

6. Emit explicit three-state rules for DeepProbLog

Each observation has probabilities for supported, refuted, and unknown. The program defines deterministic truth tables for composing those states. These rules run on categorical outcomes; the backend sums probabilities over possible outcomes while preserving shared observations.

Table 44. Complete two-input state rules from combine_states(). Source combination applies only to two eligible observations of the same proposition, after source policy checks.
ABAND(A,B)OR(A,B)evidence(A,B)
supportedsupportedsupportedsupportedsupported
supportedrefutedrefutedsupportedunknown
supportedunknownunknownsupportedsupported
refutedsupportedrefutedsupportedunknown
refutedrefutedrefutedrefutedrefuted
refutedunknownrefutedunknownrefuted
unknownsupportedunknownsupportedsupported
unknownrefutedrefutedunknownrefuted
unknownunknownunknownunknownunknown

NOT maps supported to refuted, refuted to supported, and unknown to unknown. For source combination, unknown adds no evidence; agreement preserves the informative state, and support/refutation disagreement becomes unknown with a conflict diagnostic. This operation is neither AND nor OR. Speech assertions and depicted events cannot be combined as the same proposition without explicit semantics.

The compiler does not emit direct Prolog calls such as hug(E1,X1,X2) for inference. It first grounds them into observation IDs, then emits status, node, and verdict rules. Here is the exact generated fixed-scoring program for the no-observation inventory above; all missing observations are explicitly unknown.

When enabled for an available trainable observation, the actual neural declaration is:

nn(relation_net,[tensor(features(O))],Z,[supported,refuted,unknown]) :: learned_status(O,Z).

The earlier score classifier uses frozen S/R/U scores and their logarithms. The later cached visual/audio representations are separate inputs for proposed feature classifiers; those classifiers have not been trained. Different model questions are treated as independent unless their canonical identity is identical, so exact inference does not establish calibrated probabilities.

7. Reject content the rules cannot preserve

Every input word must be linked to predicates or explicitly accounted for as functional material. Otherwise compilation returns a diagnostic and accepts no partial logical form. Counts/universal quantifiers, unresolved pronouns, modals, temporal/causal/conditional clauses, reporting/intention scope, “never,” and unhandled modifiers remain outside this fragment.

Table 45. Current compiler diagnostics rerun on the saved automatic parses; these are regression examples, not an estimate of general parser coverage.
InputDiagnostic codeExplanation
Alice waves before Bob runs.scopeTemporal, conditional, and causal clauses need an explicit extension.
Every woman wears a shirt.quantificationCounting and quantified noun phrases are outside the initial fragment.
Two women wear shirts.quantificationCounting and quantified noun phrases are outside the initial fragment.
She hugs Bob.referenceAn explicit noun phrase is required; pronoun resolution is not implemented.
Alice quickly hugs Bob.unhandled_contentThe compiler cannot yet preserve: quickly
Alice says that Bob runs.intensional_predicateAssertion, intention, and aspect need explicit scope and evidence policies.
Alice might hug Bob.modalityModal auxiliaries are outside the initial fragment.
A woman does not wear a shirt.negative_indefiniteNegation with indefinite arguments needs a richer quantifier analysis.

To compile another sentence from the project directory:

envs/probabilistic-verification/bin/python scripts/compile_verification_claim.py     --text "The aircraft is not yellow." --output /tmp/claim.json
# Add --ud-json /path/to/words.json to supply a parse without loading Stanza.
# Exit status 2 and status="unsupported" indicate an out-of-fragment claim.

Implementation map: parsing.py supplies UD records; compiler.py constructs predicates, roles, scope, and coverage; representation.py stores the logical form; logic.py grounds candidates and emits ProbLog; multimodal.py applies source eligibility and combines aligned observations; backend.py performs inference/training.

Audit compilation on real claims

Baseline audit completed · 28 October 2026. The current compiler pipeline accepts 78 of 2,375 claims (3.28%). Ordinary locations, complements, fragments and quantities are outside its effective coverage. Accepted programs also need semantic review. The compiler was frozen throughout this audit; no parser/model training or compiler fix was introduced.

Census countsAll 2,375 outcomesAll assistant reviewsReviews with exact compiler outputsFindings and recommendationsFrozen source, inputs and replayUpdated checklist

Coverage is not correctness. “Compiled” means a logical form was emitted. “Unsupported” is a compiler/input diagnostic, not a claim verdict of refuted or insufficient evidence. This experiment uses claim text and dependency parses; it does not assess whether the media supports a claim.

4. Assistant semantic review

Each review compares the claim with its actual output. Core structure means the predicate/argument/modifier reading within the restricted, tense-agnostic fragment. An adequate core does not certify full claim meaning: tense/aspect remain unencoded, and some group/context conventions need definition.

5. Concrete examples

Compiler outputs below are measured artifacts. Expected meanings and failure interpretations are assistant judgments, labeled inferred. The complete review set and original parses are downloadable.

TjHepwuhkYFA_1001

The earthquake occurred in Myanmar.

Parse/roles: in → case; Myanmar → obl

Measured compiler output: unsupported

The compiler cannot yet preserve: in, Myanmar

Expected meaning — inferred: An earthquake occurred in Myanmar.

Review — inferred: The event’s location is unhandled despite a simple clause. This is a clear ordinary-coverage gap, not evidence that the claim itself is false or unknown.

T2G_ACMxR_I4_1396

IM-1 landed on the moon.

Parse/roles: 1 → dep; on → case; the → det; moon → obl

Measured compiler output: unsupported

The compiler cannot yet preserve: 1, on, the, moon

Expected meaning — inferred: The named IM-1 vehicle landed on the moon.

Review — inferred: Here the numeral is tagged dep rather than nummod, so rejection is unhandled_content instead of quantification. The Moon location is also unhandled; identifier treatment varies with parsing context.

TjHepwuhkYFA_1080

The earthquake's impact was devastating.

Parse/roles: possess roles: owner, possession; attribute roles: holder, property

Measured compiler output: compiled

EXISTS X1: ((EXISTS X2: ((entity(X1, impact) AND entity(X2, earthquake) AND possess(X2, X1))) AND attribute(X1, devastating)))

Expected meaning — inferred: The effects of the earthquake were devastating.

Review — inferred: The genitive expresses an effect/origin relationship, but the output creates possess(earthquake,impact) with owner/possession roles and a belongs-to verbalization. This is a concrete overgeneralization of genitives as ownership.

TKCfkoNUssZI_715

Martial law troops storm the parliament building.

7. What to change next

Failure pattern — inferred: the main limit is how claim meaning is represented and preserved. Ordinary oblique arguments and fragments are rejected, while a few accepted structures overgeneralize possessives or compound modifiers. Other accepted programs depend on undefined source/content, abstract-entity or idiomatic interpretations. A successful Python call and complete word coverage do not establish a faithful semantic parse.

Table 54. Recommendations for the next semantic-parsing stage. This audit changes no compiler rule and does not claim an improved model result.
PriorityRecommendationSuccess criterionEvidence
1Define the semantic representation and compare a frozen text-model semantic parser against this baseline on development claims.Preserve argument identity, lexical compounds, genitive relations, source/content scope and tense/aspect on adjudicated examples; leave ambiguous cases explicit. Measure both coverage and correctness before claiming improvement.F1, F3, F5, F8
2Extend ordinary argument/modifier coverage and distinguish names, measurements and genuine quantities.Retain locations and complements in examples such as occurred in Myanmar and IM-1 landed on the moon. Do not improve acceptance by deleting constraints.F1, F4, F7
3Add contrastive tests and explicit event/source/abstract-entity contracts before training relation classifiers.The earthquake genitive is not ownership; martial law remains a lexical unit; depiction/quotation does not silently certify world facts; temporal forms lead to distinct evidence conditions.F5, F6, F8
4Keep input-form rejection and media-evidence uncertainty separate, and reserve independent sources for later evaluation.Fragments, metadata, multiple sentences and unresolved references have visible diagnostics. Compiler rejection is never scored as a factual refutation or insufficient-evidence prediction.F1, F4

8. Validation and limits

The replay checks 4,721 compiler outcomes against the frozen source and validates 29 recorded parser refusals separately. It verifies inventory hashes, unique IDs, exact texts, cached-token conversion, code fingerprints, and exclusion of reserved sources from review. The archived inputs permit compiler replay with Python alone; a fresh Stanza pass is not required.

No GPU, media inference, factual verification label or classifier training was used. The semantic reviews are authored by the assistant that also worked on the prototype and require independent adjudication before use as a benchmark. The accepted-program review covers development sources only. The two parser conditions have different recorded work: cached timing is compilation only; current timing includes parsing. No training-efficiency comparison is made.

The audit stage is checked off in the TODO list. View the subsequent semantic compiler comparison.

Compiler improvements: semantic roles, source scope and tense

Development result: 11 of 79 previously reviewed development claims now produce checked programs, compared with 20 for the original dependency compiler on these same claims. This is compilation coverage, not semantic accuracy. The model outputs and remaining meaning errors are shown below. The original 2,375-claim baseline and its source snapshot remain unchanged.

Recommendation: keep this compiler opt-in. The 8B parser is not ready to replace the baseline; improved representation and executable checks do not by themselves solve semantic parsing.

Here, compiled and unsupported are compiler statuses. Unsupported means the representation was declined; it does not mean the media refute the claim. No factual verdict is assigned to these real claims.

Source and CPU replayCounts and provenanceAll compiled/rejected outputsExact model prompts and responsesAssistant semantic reviewsTemporal inference tracesExecuted DeepProbLog programRegression checks

1. What changed

A frozen language model proposes a semantic representation: referents, elementary events or states, semantic roles, source content, and logical operators. Deterministic Python code checks and compiles it. The text model does not decide factual support. It receives the claim and its existing dependency analysis, with no media or fact-check labels.

Table 56. Scope of the new compiler. “Checked” means that these structural conditions pass, not that the proposed meaning is correct.
ComponentImplemented behaviorLimit
Semantic rolesA complete event tuple keeps the actor, affected entity and location together. Roles and prepositions enter evidence keys.A small set of common frames is checked; arbitrary lexical semantics still requires review.
Shared references and negationRepeated mentions share a referent. Local negation contains event existence.Quantification, unresolved pronouns, complex scope and some disjunctions are refused.
Names and compoundsNumeric names can be retained; lexical compounds such as martial law troops stay together.The model can still choose a wrong type or description.
Source/content scopeA source binds to exact embedded text, evidence route and assertion/question/depiction act.Embedded content is retained as text, not recursively decomposed. These cases are counted separately.
NormalizationRecover attached auxiliaries/prepositions and punctuation. Remove unused inner annotations only after checking the complete source-content boundary. Every change is logged.Referenced inner world predicates still cause rejection. Roles, predicates and content boundaries are not rewritten. Token coverage is not a meaning certificate.
Temporal conditionsRead the complete auxiliary chain and emit an executable tense/aspect condition with an explicit reference-context candidate.The fixed checker needs supplied episodic event-time annotations; real-video interval extraction is pending.

2. Coverage on the audited development claims

The same 50 random, 20 diagnostic and 9 additional accepted claims are used. All exclude reserved source videos. The diagnostic and additional accepted sets are selected for analysis; pooling them does not estimate corpus accuracy. One random claim, the typhoon example, is a prompt demonstration and is explicitly not an independent check.

The practical fallback uses the existing Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct checkpoint in text-only mode, float16, greedy decoding with Transformers. JSON is requested in the prompt and validated afterwards. It is not grammar-constrained decoding. The A100 request for the 30B text model was cancelled because its queue estimate was the next day; available V100s ran this comparison, at most four concurrently.

Source-scope prompt revision

Both models confused ordinary world predicates with source statements. A third prompt adds two synthetic worked examples: a photograph depicting a blue boat and a narrator saying that a ship landed. The model then produces source units, but still lists unused inner referents. The compiler removes these redundant annotations only after checking that the exact content covers the complete dependency complement. A referenced inner world predicate is still rejected. This combines a prompt revision and deterministic normalization; it is not a new evaluation set.

3. Inspect the changed programs

The following judgments compare text and logical forms. They are assistant reviews, not independent human annotations or media-support labels. Each example retains the raw model proposal and records any grammatical repair.

The typhoon is causing massive flooding. · 8B / prompt 2 · compiled

Review — adequate restricted core: The cause and effect use one complete tuple, massive modifies the same flooding referent, and the auxiliary chain adds present progressive. This exact claim is a worked prompt example, so it is not independent evidence of parser generalization.

4. What the temporal predicates mean

land(E1, theme, X1, location, X2, preposition, on) asks about one event with one spacecraft and one location. temporal(E1, past, simple, T0, required) adds a past/simple condition and a completion requirement for this landing reading. E1 is an event candidate, X1/X2 are referent candidates, and T0 is a caller-supplied discourse reference context. These are variables, not model probabilities. In the executable records, pres means present tense; simple, progressive and perfect name the aspect. A context ID enters the evidence key, so changing the reference time cannot silently reuse a score.

The four spacecraft forms produce distinct temporal predicates. The fixed checker covers a narrow episodic interval interpretation, with explicit start/end/reference times. An interval can end through interruption without completion. Perfect aspect also needs an explicit relevance/result-state annotation; past tense alone does not certify completion. Missing annotations yield unknown. This is separate from finding video time windows.

Constructed control: all non-temporal observations below are fixed to support, and all event times are supplied by us. The probabilities are actual CPU DeepProbLog outputs. They are not predictions from real video or audio.

Table 61. Executable temporal checks for four claim forms under completed, ongoing, interrupted and unannotated evidence. S = supported, R = refuted, U = unknown.
Constructed event conditionClaimReference / past referenceDeepProbLog S / R / U
completedThe spacecraft landed on the moon.10 / 2S 1 · R 0 · U 0
completedThe spacecraft is landing on the moon.10 / 2S 0 · R 1 · U 0
completedThe spacecraft was landing on the moon.10 / 2S 1 · R 0 · U 0
completedThe spacecraft has landed on the moon.10 / 2S 1 · R 0 · U 0
ongoingThe spacecraft landed on the moon.10 / 2S 0 · R 1 · U 0
ongoingThe spacecraft is landing on the moon.10 / 2S 1 · R 0 · U 0
ongoingThe spacecraft was landing on the moon.10 / 2S 1 · R 0 · U 0
ongoingThe spacecraft has landed on the moon.10 / 2S 0 · R 1 · U 0
interruptedThe spacecraft landed on the moon.10 / 2S 0 · R 1 · U 0
interruptedThe spacecraft is landing on the moon.10 / 2S 0 · R 1 · U 0
interruptedThe spacecraft was landing on the moon.10 / 2S 1 · R 0 · U 0
interruptedThe spacecraft has landed on the moon.10 / 2S 0 · R 1 · U 0
unannotatedThe spacecraft landed on the moon.missing / missingS 0 · R 0 · U 1
unannotatedThe spacecraft is landing on the moon.missing / missingS 0 · R 0 · U 1
unannotatedThe spacecraft was landing on the moon.missing / missingS 0 · R 0 · U 1
unannotatedThe spacecraft has landed on the moon.missing / missingS 0 · R 0 · U 1

A completed landing supports “landed” and can also support “was landing” at an earlier reference time. A tense swap therefore does not automatically define a false example. The same event identity and the intended reference context must be reviewed.

5. Checks, remaining failures and next actions

The word-coverage, semantic-role and temporal checks test the deterministic compiler with hand-authored semantic representations. That is separate from testing the text parser: in the generated 8B contrasts, the passive paraphrase, perfect landing clause and source statement can still be refused. Relation atoms declare an interface for small learned classifiers; no such classifier is trained in this run.

Table 62. Validation and its limits. Compilation coverage, semantic correctness and factual support are separate outcomes.
CheckMeasured result
Automated regression checks64 passed, 0 failures; includes original tests, active/passive equivalence, role/attribute changes, negation, source scope, numeric names and actual temporal DeepProbLog inference.
Frozen baseline replay4,721 original compiler outcomes replayed; 29 recorded parser refusals validated; original source hashes still match.
Generated constructed contrasts{'unsupported': 13, 'compiled': 8}; these are development diagnostics, not an independent benchmark.
Generation work99 revised-prompt requests; 44760 generated tokens; 2394.9 summed generation seconds across workers, excluding loading. This is not end-to-end wall time.
Semantic correctnessAll 11 accepted broad 8B development programs, all seven larger-model diagnostics, three revised-prompt source programs, and five diagnostic refusals were inspected. These are assistant reviews, not independent human gold. Home-run meaning and some type/role contracts remain unresolved.
  • Keep the new compiler opt-in. The broad 8B parser covers fewer selected claims than v1; a larger model alone did not fix source scope. Three targeted source fixes combine prompt revision with checked normalization and do not establish generalization.
  • Re-run the source-aware prompt and compiler on the same development inventory before expanding. Resolve genitive relations, lexical readings such as hit a home run, natural-phenomenon types and inconsistent role names; do not relax semantic checks to raise coverage.
  • Add checked dependency repairs for genuine parser errors and more scope constructions. A model proposal that conflicts with the parse should be reviewed, not silently accepted.
  • Review more accepted programs independently, freeze the selected parser/compiler on development data, and evaluate on separate source videos.
  • Extract and review real temporal observations before treating interval checks as media verification; video-window localization and relation-classifier training remain later work.

The checklist records completed compiler work and the remaining semantic review, parser repairs and held-out evaluation. Feature-classifier training stays after these checks.

Claim compilation: logical forms and interfaces

29 October: meaning preservation in compilation

The bounded SRL revision compiles 2,042/2,375 inputs. Fresh 20-case review: 8 faithful, 5 partial, 2 incorrect and 5 refused. Inspect the 24 reference readings, corrected bindings and remaining errors. Open the semantic compiler revision and next steps.

29 October follow-up: one SRL compilation path

The new experiment removes per-claim parser selection and compares a deterministic SRL/dependency compiler with separate LLM edit conditions. Coverage and meaning preservation are reported separately. Open the SRL-only census, concise prompt and paired reviews.

29 October: full 2,375-claim compilation run

The revised original-text semantic parser and scoped compiler produce 1934 executable outputs, compared with 1,544 under the previous SRL/AMR selection policy. Compilation acceptance is not semantic accuracy. Open the complete census, meaning review, failure analysis and searchable per-claim structures.

Earlier comparison: PENMAN graphs and the first shared compiler

Getting claim compilation working

Current priority: choose a reliable route from a claim to a logical form and then DeepProbLog. This comparison uses 79 previously reviewed development claims and 21 constructed controls. It performs no new media verification or relation-classifier training.

Recommendation: keep trained semantic role labeling (SRL) as the inexpensive span/role baseline and pretrained Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) as the main structured alternative. Fix their shared deterministic translation first. The next neural experiment should build a small logical form clause by clause, with deterministic serialization. The prompted 8B graphs below are not reliable enough to adopt.

Syntax still helps with alignment, verb forms and diagnostics. It need not be the structure used by probabilistic inference. A shared argument in the logical form matters more than whether it came from a dependency tree or a semantic parser. This implements the existing paper direction; it does not change the paper to a parser-training project.

2. Execution counts, separate from meaning

These are coverage measurements, not accuracy scores. A valid graph has parseable syntax and one concept per variable. A compiled program passed the restricted logical translation. Every compiled program below also parses as ProbLog. The routes use different levels of detail, so their coverage counts do not establish which one preserves meaning best.

The initial unrestricted backend sweep was stopped after a slow case. The saved comparison uses bounded subprocesses instead. Backend execution is sampled; Prolog syntax is checked for all compiled outputs. The 77 regression tests include the original 64 checks plus 13 new graph/compiler checks. Passing them does not certify generated-parser accuracy.

3. Inspect the meaning, not just the count

Ten selected cases have assistant qualitative reviews across all four routes. These are examples, not an independent human gold set or a parser-accuracy estimate. The planned full reference review covers 25 real diagnostic claims and all 21 controls.

Observed problemConcrete evidenceWhat follows
Incorrect accepted rolesFor IM-1 landed on the moon, both neural conditions use ARG0=IM-1 and ARG1=moon; the trained AMR has ARG1=IM-1 and location=moon.Predicate signatures need checking. Valid syntax is insufficient.

Landing roles and name

IM-1 landed on the moon.

Meaning to preserve: IM-1 is the lander; the moon is its location. Retain the past tense.

Trained SRL + dependency-assisted rules — compiled

The trained SRL preserves IM-1 as ARG1 and on the moon as a location phrase. The location phrase is not internally decomposed.

Generated graph
(e1 / land
    :ARG1 (x1 / entity
              :surface "IM-1")
    :ARGM-LOC (x2 / entity
                  :surface "on the moon"))
Compiled logical form
EXISTS X1, X2: ((referent(X1, IM-1) AND concept(X1, entity) AND referent(X2, on the moon) AND concept(X2, entity) AND EXISTS E1: ((land(E1, ARG1, X1, ARGM-LOC, X2) AND EXISTS T0: (temporal(E1, past, simple, T0))))))

E1 denotes an event variable, X1 an entity variable, and T0 the discourse reference context. EXISTS introduces a candidate; AND requires all conditions; NOT has the displayed scope. These are variables and operators, not probabilities.

4. What the literature changes in the plan

Table 67. Verified primary literature. These are design lessons; we have not implemented the cited systems in this comparison.
Primary sourceRelevant lesson
Wide-Coverage Semantic Analysis with Boxer (2008)Syntax is useful when paired with a defined compositional semantics; a dependency edge is not itself a logical operator.
ccg2lambda: A Compositional Semantics System (2016)A principled syntax-to-logic baseline is possible, but installing CCG and supplying lexical templates is additional work; it is not our current UD rules.
Expressive Power of Abstract Meaning Representations (2016)Do not simply conjoin every AMR triple or assume every embedded event is asserted. Our restricted translation is not an implementation of the complete formal account.
Annotation of Tense and Aspect Semantics for Sentential AMR (2018)Add source-aligned tense/aspect to AMR; landed and is landing must not collapse. This does not locate a video event.
Constrained Language Models Yield Few-Shot Semantic Parsers (2021)A small readable target language is an alternative to a large token-indexed JSON schema; its meaning still needs checking.
PICARD: Parsing Incrementally for Constrained Auto-Regressive Decoding from Language Models (2021)Grammar-constrained decoding can address formatting, but cannot guarantee correct roles, polarity or source scope. We have not implemented it in this run.
Divide and Translate: Compositional First-Order Logic Translation and Verification for Complex Logical Reasoning (2025)Clause-by-clause translation is a stronger next experiment than expanding one monolithic prompt. Solver agreement is not proof of faithfulness to a media claim.
Few-Shot Natural Language to First-Order Logic Translation via Code Generation (2025)Supports testing a short structured construction interface; never execute arbitrary model-generated Python in our compiler.
NL2LOGIC: AST-Guided Translation of Natural Language into First-Order Logic with Large Language Models (2026)Very close precedent for separating semantic parsing from deterministic compilation. That separation alone cannot be our novelty; the future paper must establish the multimodal binding/evidence contribution.

Interpretation: building a logical form and compiling it deterministically is established practice. The future paper needs its contribution in multimodal evidence assignments and binding learning. We should use established parsing techniques as infrastructure and avoid turning this into a new general-purpose semantic-parser project.

5. Updated compilation-first plan

  • ☑Specify semantic requirements for 25 real diagnostic claims and 21 controls; flag uncertain readings separately
  • ☑Implement a common JSON logical form and deterministic compiler, including recursive source content, shared referents, predicate senses and source-aligned temporal fields
  • ☑Expose simple noun-phrase modifiers and keep opaque phrases explicitly marked
  • ☑Compare trained SRL, pretrained AMR and direct/SRL-assisted frozen logical-form generation on the fixed development inputs
  • ☑Freeze before checking new source videos; preserve the first 20-source results, fix structural bugs, and evaluate on ten additional disjoint sources
  • ☑Review accepted programs as well as refusals; keep executability, diagnostic checks and meaning judgments separate
  • ☐Fix remaining criticism/reporting scope and nominal media descriptions; require complete original-claim coverage before automatic acceptance
  • ☑Define context requirements for bare names, labels, omitted subjects and underspecified measurements
  • ☐Complete wider modifier/reference coverage and rerun a frozen source-disjoint evaluation before selecting a default parser
  • ☑Freeze all 2,375 original texts; run the prior SRL/AMR compiler over every claim and retain every rejection reason
  • ☑Parse all original claims with the larger frozen text model; add scoped proposition arguments, group quantities, measurements, noun-phrase relations and explicit context requirements
  • ☑Run the revised compiler on all 2,375 claims; validate generated programs and review accepted outputs and refusals separately
  • ☑Publish per-claim outputs, full-corpus statistics and semantic failure examples; do not equate compilation with correctness
  • ☑Run one SRL/dependency clause-graph compiler on all 2,375 original inputs without candidate selection
  • ☑Compare concise token-referenced LLM edits with and without AMR on the same 48 claims; review the same 24 random cases
  • ☑Complete the bounded nominal source/prediction-scope changes and inspect remaining event-nominal identity errors
  • ☑Implement structured a/an copular/location complements and selected explicit/lexically licensed event controllers; retain broader limitations

Proposed planning limit: one or two focused working days on the remaining compilation choices, then choose the simplest adequate route and document its supported fragment. This is a planning proposal, not a promised completion time. Keep media verification and new relation training deferred.

The next neural condition should generate a small logical abstract syntax tree: a structured representation of predicates and operators, built clause by clause. Deterministic code can assign graph identifiers and emit Prolog, reducing formatting burden. Compare it with both trained SRL and pretrained AMR using the same meaning requirements. Grammar constraints improve format validity; they do not prove the translation correct.

Before selecting a front end, resolve source-content recursion, noun-phrase relationships, predicate senses and signatures, and one temporal interface. The four-argument temporal atoms in this pilot are compilation outputs; they are not connected to the earlier five-argument interval checker. Keep refusals explicit for unsupported meanings. Then freeze the parser and evaluate compilation on unseen sources, reporting faithful accepted outputs separately from wrong accepted outputs and refusals.

Measured GPU allocation: five completed one-V100 jobs, at most four concurrently, totaling 0.3336 GPU hours including loading. The real-claim SRL cache was reused; only the 21 controls required new trained-SRL CPU inference. No model was fine-tuned. Exact jobs/configuration and source references are in the downloadable artifacts.

28 October implementation: logical forms and compiler interfaces

Decision: proceed with the accepted compilation choices. LLM sentence rewriting is reserved as a last resort and has not been implemented. All experiments below parse the original claim. Further media verification and relation-model training remain deferred.

Current assessment: keep this compiler opt-in. The shared representation, recursive source content and new structural checks are implemented. Development requirements improve, but the fresh source check still exposes incorrect accepted translations and underspecified fragments. Executable output is not a certificate of preserved meaning.

What representation and interface mean

A representation here is the claim’s structured meaning, usually called a logical form: predicates, their arguments, shared referents, operators and source scopes. It is not a neural feature vector. For “Alice hugs Bob and waves,” it records two events joined by AND, the same Alice in both events, and Bob in the hug. JSON and PENMAN are ways to write a structure; the notation alone does not define its meaning.

An interface specifies a component’s inputs, outputs and their meanings. Every parser can supply the same logical-form format; the compiler turns it into variables, predicates and a DeepProbLog program. The later evidence-scoring interface will specify the relation, candidate evidence, route and features given to a scorer, and the meanings of its supported/refuted/unknown probabilities. Fixed rules and learned classifiers can use that same interface.

One original claim through the interface

The narrator says the spacecraft has not landed.

The source’s saying event stays outside negation. Landing and its negation are inside speech-content scope. The full auxiliary sequence supplies present/perfect for “has not landed.”

The assistant-authored references cover 25 real diagnostic claims and 21 controls. Five uncertain lexical/noun-phrase readings are excluded from definite diagnostic counts, leaving 21 real cases and 20 controls. Checks cover specified roles, attachment, polarity, source scope and time; they do not prove full semantic equivalence. The 20 controls include three intended refusals for counting, modality and unresolved reference.

Eight compiled out of ten is not 80% semantic accuracy. The qualitative review below found a preserved basic shared-participant example, partial translations, incorrect scope, context-dependent fragments and refusals. These are assistant judgments, not independent human gold labels.

Table 71. Review of all ten fresh cases under the fixed selection policy. Incorrect accepted translations remain visible.
Original claimReview judgmentWhat the output preserves or misses
Sunny day turns dark due to dust storm.partly preservedThe transition and dust-storm cause are present, but sunny is an ordinary day property rather than an explicitly earlier state. The dynamic reading needs review.
Lady on the screen is criticizing exiled Mexicans for not standing up to the Narco State.incorrect scopeThe criticism reason is partly kept as a phrase, but the program separately asserts a negative stand event in world scope. This is not a faithful criticism-content translation.
Man giving a speech is using a microphone. preserved for reviewThe speak and use events share the same man, and the microphone is attached to use. This satisfies the specified basic role/identity reading; full lexical equivalence is not certified.
Cannon/explosives blasting in the background.partialCannon/explosives remains one opaque phrase. The program retains blasting/background but does not resolve the noun-phrase alternatives.
FOX News.context requiredFOX News is compiled as an existing broadcast-program referent. The fragment alone does not identify whether the intended claim is about a logo, written label or organization.
Multiple aerial clips of the smoke coming from the bottom of the building.incorrect scopeClip/topic, aerial, smoke and building-bottom relations survive, but the coming-smoke event is in world scope rather than clearly inside depiction. Multiple is not a defined group quantifier.
Power outages likely in residential area.refusedBoth baselines refuse the likely-outages description; no actual outage is asserted. Modality remains unsupported.
Made landfall on the east coast of Mexico with winds at 45mph.refusedBoth baselines refuse this fragment with a speed measurement and omitted subject. The numeric guard is broader than counting; it also declines this scalar measurement.
Evening of the third shows values at 2.5.context requiredDate, ordinal and numeric value appear in the graph, but what is being measured and what shows the value are unspecified. The original context is needed.
Tik Tok Meganmarplescontext requiredThe visible label/handle is turned into a person referent. The fragment lacks the context needed to decide the intended OCR/profile assertion.

What remains before default use

  • Require complete coverage of the original claim, including nominal media/source descriptions.
  • Preserve criticism, purpose and other embedded scopes without independently asserting their contents.
  • Define how bare names, labels, omitted subjects and unspecified measurements obtain their intended claim context.
  • Extend noun-phrase, shared-reference and lexical interpretation checks; then run another frozen source evaluation.

The rewrite fallback remains reserved. A later rewrite would need to preserve roles, names, quantities, modifiers, negation, modality, tense, reference and source scope. Rephrasing cannot supply missing context without adding information. No rewriting function, prompt or fallback call is implemented.

Validation: 96 regression checks pass, including actual DeepProbLog execution with artificial unknown inputs for local negation and nested source content. All development outputs can be replayed on CPU. No media verification or new relation model was trained. See the updated checklist.

Primary references: DeepProbLog paper, official implementation, and Stanza documentation. The compiler and demonstrations here are our project implementation.
